outputs.final_proof:
\begin{proof}
Let $\{H_i\mid i\in I\}$ be a nonempty collection of normal subgroups of $G$, and define
\[
K=\bigcap_{i\in I}H_i.
\]
For each $i\in I$, the identity $e$ belongs to $H_i$, so $e\in K$. If $x,y\in K$, then $x,y\in H_i$ for every $i\in I$. Since $H_i$ is a subgroup, $xy^{-1}\in H_i$ for every $i\in I$, and hence $xy^{-1}\in K$. Therefore $K\leq G$.
Let $a\in K$ and $g\in G$. For each $i\in I$, we have $a\in H_i$ and, by normality of $H_i$, $gag^{-1}\in H_i$. It follows that $gag^{-1}\in K$. Thus $gKg^{-1}\subseteq K$ for every $g\in G$, and therefore $K\trianglelefteq G$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}
Let $\{H_i\mid i\in I\}$ be an arbitrary nonempty collection of normal subgroups of $G$, and let
\[
K:=\bigcap_{i\in I}H_i.
\]
We first verify that $K$ is a subgroup. Since $e\in H_i$ for every $i\in I$, we have $e\in K$. If $x,y\in K$, then $x,y\in H_i$ for every $i\in I$. As each $H_i$ is a subgroup, $xy^{-1}\in H_i$ for every $i\in I$, so $xy^{-1}\in K$. Hence $K\leq G$.

To verify normality, take arbitrary $g\in G$ and $a\in K$. By the definition of intersection, $a\in H_i$ for every $i\in I$. Since every $H_i$ is normal in $G$, this implies $gag^{-1}\in H_i$ for every $i\in I$. Therefore $gag^{-1}\in K$. Thus $gKg^{-1}\subseteq K$ for every $g\in G$; replacing $g$ by $g^{-1}$ gives equality, so $gKg^{-1}=K$. Consequently $K\trianglelefteq G$.
\end{proof}
